# Architecture

**Audio ownership** uses the MV3 capture lifecycle: the action identifies the source tab, a serialized service worker owns capture lifecycle, and a USER_MEDIA offscreen document owns the audio graph. Captured music plays once through a native audio element at unity volume; its Web Audio analysis branch has no playback connection. Capture explicitly requests echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain control off, checks reported settings, and stops if the browser retains processing. The analysis context uses playback latency and the reported stream sample rate. Compact features cross messages at 30 Hz, rather than PCM. Stop, source termination and viewer removal release tracks, contexts and offscreen ownership. File and capability-checked sharing routes use the same AudioOwner. No runtime remote service, account or microphone fallback is added.

**Musical motion** combines sustained level/band/trend activity with each layer's band. Every layer receives activity between beats. Shared three-axis deformation bends strands and sheets internally; fold, twist and ripple use local coordinates. Onsets rotate marks and modestly change their size. Mark color, black-floor decisions and presence have no audio dependence. Analysis remains at 30 Hz, while drawing interpolates the two most recent GPU position buffers on every display frame, with one analysis tick of latency. Categorical glyph IDs are never interpolated.

**Regular worlds and Discovery** use the unchanged 32-operator vocabulary and authored IDs. Authored placement, stable sampled world envelopes and closer cameras emphasize broad spatial structures. Discovery 1.1.0 generates landscapes, tunnels, archways, asteroid fields, orbital passages and crossings, with quality rejection for extent, visibility, crowding and insufficient screen span. It changes construction, relationships, placement and mappings. It does not merely recolor authored scenes. Sampling and validation remain bounded; no eval or executable presets are accepted.

**Polygon spaces** reconstruct retained licensed geometry offline: OSM footprint extrusions, Freedoom sector/portal surfaces, Kenney house instances and decoded terrain. Each tour stores 8,192 area/route-weighted points, local normals and surface classes in 14-byte quantized records. A guided closed spline and matching deformation of the camera maintain travel through the flexing surface. Static point fabrics avoid runtime mesh parsing, geographic requests, triangle searches and CPU vertex scans. Camera routes are artistic and have no collision-simulation guarantee.

**Spherical video** matches local source-image patches offline against the exact masks. Nine images per study encode categorical glyph IDs and RGB565 source colors in 256×64 cells covering every longitude and latitude; an opening heading rotates the panorama without cropping it. The draw budget remains capped at 8,000 marks. The GPU reads the local image fabric, maps it to a complete 360° sphere and adds continuous musical bending. Source frames run as slow forward/reverse studies, with complete automatic camera turns and unrestricted horizontal dragging. They are 360° source sequences, not native stereo VR180, full-length movie playback or inferred depth. Every study has a distinct original source video, with source metadata and frame hashes retained.

**Glyph drawing** uses GPU transform feedback for persistent form state, positions and colors, then opaque instanced bitmap quads with depth testing. Regular and polygon form matching uses canonical coverage, centroid, occupancy and orientation descriptors, plus dwell and hysteresis. Video matching uses actual local image coverage with temporal bias. The atlas retains exactly the original 8×16 masks, order, aspect and Void. No font, extra glyphs, alpha, glow or trails replace the marks.

**Color composition** belongs to the scene. Regular layers carry bounded color roles, with height/strand/facet bands evaluated in resting coordinates. Polygon ground, facades, roofs, ceilings and terrain bands use distinct anchors. Video color follows the source image. This retains recognizable placement through geometric deformation. A worker prepares the curated palette and exact finite lookup; source grading precedes treatment and quantization. True Color bypasses finite quantization. Numeric hue/shade binning avoids GPU half-boundary rounding differences. Nearest bitmap/display sampling, disabled dithering and antialiasing, and no blending preserve finite output.

**Show and retention** separate visual banks from playback choices. The default show alternates Regular with spatial scenes, shuffling Polygon and Video in pairs through the spatial slots and traversing each scene bank completely without repeats within its cycle; Discovery requires an explicit mode or action. Automatic scenes shuffle palettes by default, with a toggle. The optional regular/Discovery MixedScheduler retains elapsed viewing-time accounting, with Hold, Pause, manual and hidden-time exclusions. Upcoming assets are prefetched; the previous frame remains while a palette or source fabric loads. Request tokens prevent stale asynchronous uploads after a replacement or disposal. Forty history scenes, bounded favorites, up to 100 saved Discoveries, preferences and validated JSON import/export remain local. Spatial exports contain whitelisted bundled view references, not arbitrary paths or URLs.

**Fullscreen immersion** uses a 2.3-second inactivity timer independent of animation and Pause. Every overlay becomes transparent, hidden and inert; the cursor and dialog backdrop disappear. Pointer, keyboard, wheel or input interaction reveals the UI and restores prior inert state. Native fullscreen still requires device qualification.

Quality adapts internal resolution, draw cadence and sample budgets without changing the alphabet or finite palette. Per-layer GPU buffers cap at 8,000 marks; maximum layer count is five. Shader programs and texture allocations remain constant. Local bundle and decoded-fabric caches have explicit bounds; playback does not retain every source world. Development readbacks, importers, Playwright, Sharp and Python libraries are absent from runtime requirements.
